title: Weather & Sky
description: Grade 1 Science: weather and the sky! Kinds of weather, day and night sky, dressing for the weather, where rain comes from, and the seasons — interactive and fun.

topics.title: Kinds of Weather
topics.concept:
Weather is what the air and sky are like outside right now. It can change from day to day:

  • ☀️ Sunny — bright and warm.
  • 🌧️ Rainy — water falls from the clouds.
  • ☁️ Cloudy — grey clouds cover the sun.
  • 💨 Windy — the air moves and pushes things around.
  • ❄️ Snowy — soft white snow falls (in very cold places).

recap: Weather is what the sky and air are like outside.
Kinds of weather: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, snowy.
Weather can change from day to day.

wonder.text: When you wake up, you look outside. What is the weather like today?

qa.q: Can the weather change in one day?
qa.a: Yes! A morning can be sunny and the afternoon cloudy or rainy. That is why we check the weather before going out.

qa.q: Why is there no snow where I live?
qa.a: Snow only falls in very cold places or high mountains. In warm places like most of India, rain falls instead of snow.

topics.title: The Sky by Day and Night
topics.concept:
The sky looks very different in the day and at night:

  • ☀️ In the day, we see the bright Sun. The sky is light and blue.
  • 🌙 At night, we see the Moon and twinkling stars. The sky is dark.

The Sun gives us light and warmth. We must never look straight at the Sun — it is too bright for our eyes!
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 155" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="155" fill="#fff"/><rect x="10" y="14" width="146" height="124" rx="14" fill="#dff0ff"/><text x="50" y="78" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle">☀️</text><text x="106" y="78" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle">☁️</text><text x="83" y="120" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Day sky</text><rect x="164" y="14" width="146" height="124" rx="14" fill="#0b1437"/><text x="204" y="78" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle">🌙</text><text x="260" y="78" font-size="36" text-anchor="middle">⭐</text><text x="237" y="120" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Night sky</text></svg>
recap: Day sky: the bright Sun, light and blue.
Night sky: the Moon and stars, dark.
Never look straight at the Sun.

wonder.text: The Sun lights up the day. What lights up the night sky?

qa.q: Where does the Sun go at night?
qa.a: The Sun does not really go away! Our Earth slowly spins, so our side turns away from the Sun. That is when it becomes night for us.

qa.q: Why do stars only come out at night?
qa.a: Stars are always there! But in the day the Sun is so bright that we cannot see them. When the sky goes dark, the stars appear.

topics.title: Dressing for the Weather
topics.concept:
We choose our clothes to match the weather so we stay comfy and safe:

  • ☀️ Sunny — light clothes, a sun hat and a water bottle.
  • 🌧️ Rainy — a raincoat and an umbrella to stay dry.
  • ❄️ Cold — a warm sweater, gloves and a cap.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 155" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="155" fill="#eef6ff"/><text x="55" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">🧢</text><text x="55" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Sunny</text><text x="165" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">☂️</text><text x="165" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Rainy</text><text x="275" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">🧥</text><text x="275" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Cold</text><text x="165" y="142" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Dress for the weather</text></svg>
recap: We dress to match the weather.
Sunny → light clothes + hat; Rainy → raincoat + umbrella.
Cold → warm sweater, gloves and cap.

wonder.text: Would you wear a warm woolly coat on a hot sunny day? Why not?

qa.q: Why do we wear light clothes when it is hot?
qa.a: Light, loose clothes help our body stay cool and let the heat escape. Heavy clothes would trap the heat and make us too hot.

qa.q: Why carry an umbrella on a cloudy day?
qa.a: Grey clouds full of water often mean rain is coming. Carrying an umbrella keeps you ready and dry if it starts to rain.

topics.title: Where Does Rain Come From?
topics.concept:
Rain comes from a wonderful journey that water makes, again and again. It is called the water cycle:

  • ☀️ The Sun warms the water in seas, rivers and lakes.
  • 💨 The warm water rises up into the air as tiny invisible drops (vapour).
  • ☁️ High up it cools and gathers into clouds.
  • 🌧️ When the clouds are full and heavy, the water falls back down as rain.

recap: Sun warms water → it rises → clouds form → rain falls.
The same water is used again and again.

wonder.text: Rain falls from the clouds — but how did the water get up there?

qa.q: Does the same water get used again and again?
qa.a: Yes! The water that falls as rain flows back to the rivers and seas, then rises again to make new clouds. It is a never-ending cycle.

qa.q: Why do clouds look white and grey?
qa.a: Clouds are made of tiny water drops. Thin clouds look white, but when they fill up with lots of water they look dark grey — and that means rain is near!

topics.title: The Seasons
topics.concept:
A season is a time of year with its own kind of weather. In India we mainly have three big seasons:

  • ☀️ Summer — hot and sunny. We eat ice cream and drink lots of water.
  • 🌧️ Monsoon (Rainy) — lots of rain. Everything turns green.
  • ❄️ Winter — cool and cold. We wear warm clothes.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 155" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="155" fill="#fff7ea"/><text x="55" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">☀️</text><text x="55" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Summer</text><text x="165" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">🌧️</text><text x="165" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Monsoon</text><text x="275" y="68" font-size="38" text-anchor="middle">❄️</text><text x="275" y="114" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Winter</text><text x="165" y="142" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">The seasons</text></svg>
recap: A season is a time of year with its own weather.
India's main seasons: summer, monsoon (rainy), winter.
Seasons happen as Earth travels around the Sun.

wonder.text: Some months are hot, some are cold, and some are full of rain. These are the seasons!

qa.q: Why do we have different seasons?
qa.a: As the Earth travels around the Sun through the year, different times bring different weather — giving us hot, rainy and cold seasons.

qa.q: Why do farmers love the monsoon?
qa.a: The monsoon rain fills the rivers and waters the fields, helping crops like rice grow. No rain would mean less food, so farmers welcome the monsoon!

questions.q: What do we see in the sky during the day?
questions.explanation: In the day we see the bright Sun and a light blue sky.

questions.q: What should you carry on a rainy day?
questions.explanation: An umbrella keeps you dry in the rain.
When clouds get full of water, rain falls from them.
Winter is the cold season — we wear warm clothes.

questions.q: What lights up the night sky?
questions.explanation: The Moon and stars light up the dark night sky.
We must never look straight at the Sun — it is too bright and can hurt our eyes.

questions.q: Put in order — what happens FIRST to make rain?
questions.explanation: First the Sun warms the water; then it rises, clouds form, and rain falls.

questions.q: Why can't we see stars in the daytime?
questions.explanation: Stars are always there, but the Sun is so bright in the day that we cannot see them.

questions.q: Why does the Sun seem to disappear at night?
options: The Earth spins away from it
questions.explanation: The Earth spins, turning our side away from the Sun — that makes night.
Dark grey clouds are full of water, so rain is likely on the way.

questions.q: Why do farmers welcome the monsoon?
questions.explanation: Monsoon rain waters the fields and helps crops like rice grow.
